configurePresets.name: debug-og
configurePresets.description: Debug at -Og instead of CMake's default Debug (-g, i.e. -O0): keeps -g and asserts but drops the -O0 slowdown on compute-heavy tests. Coverage deliberately does NOT use this — it needs -O0 for accurate line data.

configurePresets.name: lib-release
configurePresets.description: Library-only build (no tests/examples) at the x86-64-v3 baseline — shared by the binding jobs. Build type defaults to Release.

configurePresets.name: ci-linux-debug
configurePresets.description: Plain -Og Debug: full build + test suite, no runtime sanitizers. Used by the GCC Debug rows (compiler-portability coverage); GCC+ASan instrumentation of the template-heavy eval TUs exhausts the hosted runner's memory.

configurePresets.name: ci-linux-debug-asan
configurePresets.description: ci-linux-debug + ASan/UBSan. Used by the clang Debug rows only — clang's sanitizer instrumentation compiles the same TUs in a fraction of GCC's time/memory.

configurePresets.name: ci-windows
configurePresets.description: MSVC (cl.exe) via Ninja, not the Visual Studio generator: Ninja is much faster and matches every other platform's single-config flow. Needs the MSVC environment (setup-cpp vcvarsall) on PATH so CMake finds cl.exe.

configurePresets.name: ci-windows-clang
configurePresets.description: clang-cl via Ninja for compile + test coverage of the Windows clang path. Warnings-as-errors is OFF here: clang-cl turns on a broad set of -Weverything-family warnings by default (unsafe-buffer-usage, exit-time-destructors, ...) that the plain clang driver does not, so -Werror would gate on clang-cl quirks rather than real issues. Warning hygiene for our chosen flag set is already enforced under -Werror by the five Linux clang rows; this row verifies the code compiles and the tests pass under clang-cl. Needs the MSVC environment (setup-cpp vcvarsall) on PATH.

configurePresets.name: coverage
configurePresets.description: Plain Debug (-O0), NOT debug-og: -O0 is what makes gcov line coverage accurate.

configurePresets.name: valgrind
configurePresets.description: Single-arch (multiarch off by default) so valgrind never has to execute the AVX-512 dispatch variant it can't handle.

configurePresets.name: multiarch
configurePresets.displayName: Multiarch dispatch (x86-64 baseline + runtime ISA select)
configurePresets.description: TREEWEAVE_ARCH=x86-64 (not v3): the dispatcher builds every ISA variant and picks one at runtime, so the compile baseline must be the lowest.

configurePresets.name: multiarch-arm
configurePresets.displayName: Multiarch dispatch (aarch64 armv8-a baseline + runtime ISA select)
configurePresets.description: aarch64 counterpart of multiarch: TREEWEAVE_ARCH=armv8-a so the compile baseline is the portable ARMv8-A level; the dispatcher selects the single mandatory neon64 variant at runtime (SVE excluded by design).

configurePresets.name: codspeed
configurePresets.description: Instruction-count perf bench for CodSpeed CI. x86-64-v3 (AVX2) baseline is deliberate: CodSpeed `simulation` runs the binary under Valgrind/Cachegrind, which handles AVX2 but not AVX-512 — same constraint as the `valgrind` preset. RelWithDebInfo keeps the debug symbols CodSpeed needs for meaningful reports.

configurePresets.name: bindings-matlab
configurePresets.description: Builds the MEX entirely from CMake: fetches the mwrap generator via CPM, generates the gateway + bz_*.m from treeweave.mw, and compiles/links treeweave_c_static via matlab_add_mex (MATLAB) and/or mkoctfile (Octave).

configurePresets.name: bindings-octave
configurePresets.description: Alias of bindings-matlab for the license-free CI path: with only mkoctfile present, the binding builds the Octave MEX (treeweave_mex.mex) via mwrap + mkoctfile.
